articles.author: Diff Guru
articles.description:
You have two JSON objects. Maybe one is a response from your production API, and the other is from staging. You want to see if the data has changed. You paste them into a standard text diff tool, and the entire screen lights up red.
Why? Because one API server serialized the keys as {"id": 1, "name": "Alice"} and the other did {"name": "Alice", "id": 1}.
To a computer doing a text comparison, these strings are completely different. To a human (and your application logic), they are identical.
This frustration is why I built the JSON Diff & Validator tool at Diff Guru. Here is why standard text diffs fail at JSON, and how we solved it.
Standard diff algorithms (like the Myers difference algorithm) work linearly. They compare sequences of characters or lines. They don't understand structure.
…
articles.title: Stop Using Text Diff for JSON: A Better Way to Compare Objects
